headline: Client Monday opens with a live buyer on the board — 355 Comanche came back INTERESTED = YES with one word attached, 'too high' — and two houses get walked before 1:15 · DO: text Nicole W. on 683 Flag, which day and where is the addendum · WATCH: the lead webhook is still dead at ~70 hours, four named leads have now fallen in that hole.

notes: ✅ THE BEST MONDAY MORNING THE FLEET HAS PRODUCED IN TWO WEEKS. Nine routines fired clean before 7:30 — marketing 5:05, inbox triage 5:53, Money Pulse 6:05, The Daily 6:42, the Money Machine 6:45, the weekly pipeline 7:00, listing folder sync 7:06, team daily 7:20 — with ZERO blocked lines in 24 hours. And the ISA lane did the thing it exists to do: two D0s went out at 7:00 and 7:01 to the two newest ad leads, inside an hour of the window opening.

🎉 THE ROUTINE THIS BOARD HAS CALLED BUILD #1 FOR THREE STRAIGHT WEEKS ACTUALLY RAN. Weekly Pipeline & Forecast fired at 7:00 and did real work — it confirmed 21 closings off seven Payday receipts and reconciled the 21-versus-24 disagreement this board printed as an open discrepancy last night. ⚠️ ONE HALF OF THE BUG SURVIVES: it staged its output as a DRAFT and did not send. So the number is finally settled and the email still has not landed in your inbox.

🛑 STILL EXACTLY ONE THING GENUINELY DEAD, AND IT IS STILL THE EXPENSIVE ONE. The Brivity instant-lead webhook has been off since Friday 9:32 AM — now roughly 70 hours — and a direct search this run confirms it: zero lead alerts and zero Make notices in 48 hours, and the instant responder has written no heartbeat line for four days. That is why this panel reads alert and not ok. Four named leads have now arrived to silence. ⛔ DO NOT SIMPLY SWITCH IT BACK ON — 243 errors in five minutes is what deactivated it. Read the execution log first.

callBlock.who: The dead lead webhook — now four named leads deep, three days with nothing answering (ops, not a person)
callBlock.why: 🛑 THE ONLY THING ON THIS BOARD STILL ACTIVELY BLEEDING, AND THE COST NOW HAS FOUR NAMES ON IT. The Brivity instant-lead scenario has been off since Friday 9:32 AM — roughly 70 hours — and it is both the instant responder's ONLY input and the first rung of the ownership check. ⭐ RE-CONFIRMED THIS MORNING RATHER THAN CARRIED FORWARD: a direct search returned zero lead alerts and zero Make stop-or-error notices in the last 48 hours, and the responder has written no heartbeat line since Thursday. ⚠️ THE PART THAT SHOULD STILL BOTHER YOU IS THE SILENCING, NOT THE OUTAGE: a p1 raised this correctly on Friday and was checked off Saturday with the scenario still dead. The alarm was answered by closing the alarm. ⛔ DO NOT JUST FLIP IT ON — 243 errors in five minutes reads like a payload or mapping change, and that storm is what killed it. Open the execution history first or it deactivates itself again inside the hour. ⭐ ONE PIECE OF GOOD NEWS: the leads are NOT being lost, only unanswered — every one of the four was caught by hand and has a chip on this list.

callBlock.who: Sondra & Darrell S. — a buy and a list in one message, and the ball has sat in her court since Friday
callBlock.why: 🔥 STILL THE CLEANEST AT-BAT ON THE BOARD AND IT IS BOTH SIDES OF A DEAL. Friday 5:02 PM, unprompted, off an automated listing alert: "We are very interested in this property! I think we are about ready to put ours on the market also! If you have time, we would love to get with you ASAP." ✅ You answered yourself at 5:33 and copied him exactly as she asked. ⚠️ BUT THAT REPLY PUT THE NEXT MOVE ON HER AND SHE ASKED FOR THE OPPOSITE. She used the word ASAP and already said she was ready; a standing offer is not a calendar invite, and it is now four days old with nothing back. ⭐ IT IS ALSO CLIENT-DAY WORK IN THE PUREST SENSE — the call proposes a specific time and does both sides in one trip: walk the Helena house she flagged, then walk theirs. The buy side is the two-bathroom setup they told you in March they needed. ⚠️ CALL, DO NOT TEXT — the record shows Agent Referral as the source, so there is no consent trail for a text. ⚠️ A draft to her is sitting staged in the queue this morning; the phone is the better instrument on a four-day-old ASAP.

callBlock.who: Cheryl G. — the appointment is settled, and the list she asked for five days ago still hasn't gone
callBlock.why: ✅ NOTHING IS OWED ON THE APPOINTMENT AND THAT AMBIGUITY IS FULLY DEAD. She cancelled Saturday night in her own words and you answered Sunday morning asking for another day, so scheduling is legitimately in her court. ⭐ WHAT IS STILL OWED IS OLDER AND IT IS THE THING THAT ACTUALLY MOVES HER. On 7/29 she pivoted to Mt Laurel, not much above $600,000, and you answered "will start working on that now — any must haves?" That question has hung since Wednesday and the list has never gone out. She just cancelled a showing on a house she found herself; two or three real Mt Laurel options is what makes the rebook happen instead of waiting on her to raise her hand a third time. ⚠️ Her own behaviour supports the number — average view price is well above what she stated, so the ceiling is softer than she said. ⚠️ AND NOBODY HAS EVER ASKED whether her own house has to sell first, which is the single question that changes what you send her.

callBlock.who: David C. — the machine's email promised him a call, and that promise is now four days old
callBlock.why: 🔥 AN UNKEPT SAME-DAY PROMISE MADE IN YOUR NAME, NOW PAST A FULL WEEKEND AND INTO MONDAY. He registered Friday morning off the 1709 Fieldstone ad, the responder wrote him at 2:16 PM, and that email says you'll call him. Two emails out, zero replies back. ⚠️ ON A FIRST TOUCH THIS IS THE MOST EXPENSIVE KIND OF MISS, because the broken promise is the only impression he has of you. ⭐ AND THE REASON TO DIAL HIM TODAY IS BETTER THAN IT WAS YESTERDAY: the exact listing he raised his hand about has a buyer walking it at 12:45 this afternoon and a THIRD buyer walking it tomorrow morning. The house he asked about is visibly, demonstrably moving. ⭐ Ownership was verified the hard way — read live in the leads index rather than inferred from a webhook verdict — so this is genuinely yours. ⚠️ No text has gone out; his person page wedged when the sweep tried.

callBlock.who: Ashley S. — brand-new buyer lead from last night, and her only email is a relay that probably bounces
callBlock.why: 🆕 SHE LANDED SUNDAY 8:36 PM off an IDX registration on your own site — buyer intent, with a live phone she submitted herself. ⚠️ THE REASON SHE IS A CALL AND NOT AN EMAIL: her only address on file is an Apple hide-my-email relay, and this system has already met one of those and written it down as a bouncer. She has no second address. So the email channel here is probably dead on arrival and the phone is the primary instrument, not the backup. ⭐ SHE IS INBOUND AND GAVE US THE NUMBER, so one first-touch text is clean as well. ⚠️ RULE 0 IS NOT PAID AND CANNOT BE PAID THE FAST WAY — the webhook that normally settles ownership is the thing that is down, and the lead pond resolves to the same account fields Gene's own records do, so an API match is necessary and not sufficient. Read the Assigned-To block on her person page before any outbound. 🛑 She is the fourth named lead to fall in the dead-webhook hole, and the second carrying a live phone — which is what turns the outage from a latency cost into a missed dial.

callBlock.who: Lisa S. — fourth name off one ad in four days, and her first email went out at 7:00 this morning
callBlock.why: ✅ THE MACHINE DID ITS HALF ON TIME FOR ONCE — the D0 went out at 7:00:51 AM, inside an hour of the send window opening, on a lead that landed 7:47 last night. That is the shape this lane is supposed to have. ⭐ WHAT IS LEFT IS THE CALL, AND THE AD STORY IS WHY IT MATTERS. She is the FOURTH name off the 1709 Fieldstone ad in four days — and of those four, not one has had an actual conversation. The ad is producing and the conversations are not happening; that gap is the whole finding. ⚠️ NOT ASSERTED: that any of the three showings now booked on that listing is attributable to any of these four. A showing is booked by a co-op agent; an ad lead is a consumer click. Two different funnels that happen to share an address. ⚠️ RULE 0 sits at the same place Ashley's does — the API cannot distinguish pond from assigned, so read the Assigned-To block before anything further goes out. ⭐ She is TCPA-clear for one first-touch text as an inbound registrant.

callBlock.who: Anthony M. — third lead off the same ad, re-engaged Sunday afternoon, and he has never once been touched
callBlock.why: ⭐ THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN HIM AND THE OTHER THREE IS THAT HE IS NOT NEW — he is an EXISTING record who came back and re-engaged with your ad Sunday at 4:30 PM. A lead returning on their own is a warmer signal than a first click, and it landed nineteen minutes after a showing was confirmed on that same listing. ⚠️ AND HE HAS ZERO TOUCHES, VERIFIED BOTH DIRECTIONS — a token search of the ledger returned nothing on his name, and an all-time both-alias mail pull on his address returned nothing at all. Never contacted, ever. ⭐ THE INSTRUMENT IS A WRITTEN TOUCH, NOT A DIAL — the re-engaged lane maps to a drafted email, and the rule on it is firm: NEVER cite the click. "You crossed my desk again" energy, one piece of real market value, one soft question. ⚠️ RULE 0 unpaid, same as the other two: the hidden footer in that notice carries the right account id and that still proves nothing, because it renders identically on pond records.

callBlock.who: Chris R. — a listing referral from another Real agent, dark six months, and the only clean number on the overdue board
callBlock.why: ⭐ THIS IS THE ONE OVERDUE NAME THAT SURVIVED A DNC AUDIT, AND THAT IS WHY IT IS HERE. Sunday's deep sweep ran the top four overdue seller-intent names to their person pages and checked every line: three of the four are do-not-call on their only number or run on purchased data. His line is clean. ⚠️ WHAT MAKES IT COST MORE THAN A LEAD: this is a referral FROM another Real Broker agent. You spoke with the customer, then it went quiet for six months and the appointment task went overdue. The lead is one conversation; the referral relationship is the recurring asset, and it is the half that is actually decaying. ⭐ An out-of-state area code on an Alabama house reads absentee owner, which is usually a straightforward listing if he still owns it. ⚠️ Honest caveat: the property scores low to sell and six months is long enough that it may already have happened. Both answers are worth having, and only the call produces either. ⚠️ No email drafted deliberately — six months of silence is a call, not a first email.

listings.status: 🔥 Active $299K — INTERESTED = YES came back at 5:55 last night, with 'too high' attached
listings.note: 🔥 THE BEST AND HARDEST THING ON YOUR BOARD THIS MORNING, AND IT ARRIVED FOUR HOURS AFTER YOUR LETTER WENT OUT. Angela B. of Keller Williams Realty Vestavia answered yesterday's 1:15 showing at 5:55 PM: interested — YES · priced right — TOO HIGH · price recommendation — BLANK · staged — 4, the highest staging score this listing has ever recorded · and verbatim on what drove it: "Saw another home that she is interested in." ⭐ AN INTERESTED BUYER WHO SAYS THE PRICE IS TOO HIGH IS THE MOST USEFUL THING THIS LISTING HAS PRODUCED. She did not walk on condition, layout or location — she liked it and priced it against an alternative. That is a live buyer you can still lose to a number. 🔥 AND IT IS THE THIRD INDEPENDENT PRICE READ POINTING THE SAME WAY: 7/25 feedback said too high, the only written offer this house ever produced was $280,000 against a $299,000 ask from a buyer papered at exactly $280,000, and now this. One form is noise; three plus an offer is a market. ⚠️ NOBODY HAS EVER NAMED A REPLACEMENT NUMBER — every price-recommendation field on all three came back blank. Do not invent one from these, and do not quote a counter figure; two conflicting numbers sit on file and neither is clean. ⭐ THE TIMING IS THE ARGUMENT FOR THE CALL: your 1:38 letter told Seth you'd know after the showing landed. It landed. Ask for the pricing conversation, don't hold it on the doorstep. ⚠️ Yesterday's 3:44 preview read — not interested, both price fields blank, "poor lighting in several rooms" — is a DIFFERENT agent on a DIFFERENT visit and says the opposite. Do not merge them; the staging 4 quietly retires the lighting note as the headline problem, but the bulbs are still thirty dollars.

listings.note: 🔥 THE DEMAND CURVE ON THIS HOUSE TURNED LAST NIGHT AND IT IS WORTH SAYING OUT LOUD ON THE CLIENT-DAY CALL. It held exactly ONE tour in its first eleven days — then booked its SECOND and THIRD inside seven hours: Julie B. of Southern Elite at 4:09 PM for TODAY 12:45–1:45, and Tammy M. of eXp Realty at 6:44 PM for TOMORROW 10:00–11:00. Three different brokerages, three first-time lookers. ⚠️ THE OPERATIONAL FACT THAT NOW MATTERS TWICE: the Hulseys are OWNER-OCCUPANTS and have to clear the house on TWO CONSECUTIVE DAYS — out by about 12:30 today and about 9:45 tomorrow. ⭐ GIVE THEM BOTH TIMES IN ONE MESSAGE, NOT TWO, and use the same call to deliver the Saturday open-house debrief they still have not had. This is the healthiest client relationship on the board — you wrote them Friday night and got "Sounds good Thanks" back. 🔴 THE BOARD STILL CANNOT TELL YOU HOW SATURDAY WENT, and that is blindness rather than failure — the open house ran 3–5 while the fleet was dark, and no traffic count, sign-in sheet or debrief was captured by anything. ⚠️ AND THE LOCKBOX ITEM, UNCLOSED BY ANY RECEIPT SINCE 7/20, NOW GATES THREE SHOWINGS INSTEAD OF ONE. The 7/30 tour running implies a box was on the door; it does not prove one is there now. Cheapest thing on this file to go verify, most expensive to assume. ⚠️ The first showing's read is now four days old and still has not been asked for directly. 🔥 The ad engine is still the real story: four named leads in four days, and none of them has had a conversation yet.

listings.status: 🔥 Active $164K — second buyer walks at 1:00 TODAY, Saturday's read still owed
listings.note: 🔴 SATURDAY'S SHOWING IS NOW 46 HOURS OLD WITH NO READ, AND THE CLOCK ON IT EXPIRES AT 1:00 THIS AFTERNOON. It ran inside the dark window so nothing was watching for the feedback and nothing chased it. Whatever Saturday's buyer said is the cheapest possible prep for the one walking the same door in a few hours — after 1:00 it stops being prep and becomes history. ⭐ ASK THAT AGENT DIRECTLY, NOT THROUGH THE FORM. One direct email produced a five-minute reply on the $1.15M listing after twenty-four hours of ShowingTime silence; that is still the most transferable lesson on this board and it is still not being applied fast enough. ⭐ ONE CHEAP FIX BEFORE 1:00: the 7/14 buyer really liked this unit and the only thing he flagged was PUDDLING in the little patio area after touring in pouring rain. Check the grading and the downspout — a thirty-dollar problem reads as a water problem to a buyer. ✅ QUOTE $164,000 — both recent notices carry the MLS line verbatim, so the $5,000 cut is verified live off a primary source twice over and the hedge is retired. ⚠️ The 7/20 6:00 PM showing has now gone fourteen days with no feedback; form re-asks have produced nothing. ⚠️ The listing-agreement expiry date still does not exist anywhere in your email — pull it from the portal or just ask your seller what he signed. ✅ 92 days, still the most-shown listing on the board, and every recent read points AWAY from price.

listings.note: ✅ THE CLOSE DATE IS RECEIPTED RATHER THAN INFERRED and the closing attorney is now named on file, so no routine has to hunt for it again. THE AGREED NUMBER INSIDE IT HAS STILL NEVER BEEN READ BY ANYONE. ⚠️ The buyer side swapped transaction coordinators mid-deal, and a handoff eleven days out is exactly where documents get dropped. 🟢 The appraisal is now six days dark — longer than comfortable, still not evidence of a problem, and no low-appraisal read may be carried without a receipt. ⭐ WHAT IS ACTUALLY LEFT ON THIS CLIENT IS THE REFERRAL — the roughly $1M buyer he handed you is now day seven with no name, number or email, and it has a 12:30 block on today's calendar. ⭐ And there is still a live backup buyer from 7/21 nobody has called.

listings.status: 🎉 Under contract — signed 7/31, close date STILL not pulled, fifth ask
listings.note: 🔴 THE CLOSE DATE IS THE ONLY THING LEFT AND THIS IS THE FIFTH CONSECUTIVE BOARD SAYING SO. Your own words to your coordinator Sunday afternoon: "we went under contract 7/31, both sellers signed, and the transaction record still has no close date" — and you called it the thing holding up the forecast. ⚠️ THREE NUMBERS ARE LOCKED INSIDE THE CONTRACT AND UNREAD BY ANY ROUTINE: the executed price, the close date, and the co-op commission — the buyer's agent asked for 3.5% AND THAT HAS NEVER BEEN RULED ON. ⛔ DO NOT QUOTE A PRICE, A DATE OR A CO-OP FIGURE ON THIS FILE until someone opens the documents. Four different figures moved across 48 hours and not one is receipted; the ones that circulated were your own counters at two different hours, never the deal. ⭐ WITH 5167 NOW CONFIRMED AT 8/14, THIS IS THE ONLY NEAR-TERM DEAL WITHOUT A DATE — which makes a five-minute portal lookup the single highest-value administrative act available to you, and the milestone engine cannot arm a closing watch on this address until it exists. 🎉 THE CLIENT SIDE IS FULLY HANDLED and worth remembering on Client Day: both sellers completed Friday, and the congratulations-and-what-happens-next letter went out that evening walking the earnest money, the inspection window and the financing and appraisal clocks.

listings.note: ⏰ YOU HOSTED IT PERSONALLY 1–3 YESTERDAY AND NOTHING HAS REPORTED ON IT — no traffic count, no sign-ins, no debrief, and now a full night has passed. That is the second open house in three days this board cannot see inside of, and unlike Saturday's there is no dark-window excuse: it simply has not been written down. The objection is ACREAGE. On a $1.15M listing whose first read could have been "too expensive," a land-fit loss is the cheapest possible one — so the question worth answering off Sunday's traffic is who the buyer is that wants THIS land. ⭐ THAT ANSWER CAME FROM ONE DIRECT EMAIL IN FIVE MINUTES after the form produced nothing in twenty-four hours — still the most transferable lesson on this board, and there are two owed reads this morning it applies to directly. ⚠️ ONE HONEST DEDUCTION THAT STANDS: that buyer had already seen the property with another agent, so the first-ever showing was not a first look and the true unique-buyer count is lower than the tour count suggests. 🛑 The security item on this address is unchanged and still stands: the lookalike meeting link is not to be opened, on any device.

listings.note: 🔴 THE OLDEST UNDELIVERED PIECE OF GOOD NEWS ON THE BOARD, NOW THREE DAYS OLD AND THROUGH AN AFTERNOON WHERE NINE OTHER EMAILS WENT OUT. That makes it a choice, not a capacity problem. Lead with the price answer, not the no. ⚠️ ShowingTime's "Publish to Seller" is unclicked, so nothing reached him automatically — the read is yours to deliver or it does not get delivered. ✅ His email is on file off the MLS record now, so a written follow-up is possible for the first time and the old call-only note is retired. 🔴 The other half is day ten: the nudge to the 7/25 showing agent has never been answered. She left a note in the app, so there is genuinely something to collect — stop sending form reminders and write to her directly.
